business_model.claim: UVE is a holding company that sells personal residential property and casualty insurance—including homeowners, renters/tenants, condo unit owners, dwelling/fire, and related coverages—predominantly to consumers, along with insurance-related services.
quotes: We develop, market, and underwrite insurance products for consumers predominantly in the personal residential homeowners lines of business and perform substantially all other insurance-related services for our primary insurance entities, including risk management, claims management, and distribution.

UPCIC, our primary risk-bearing insurance entity, which accounts for the substantial majority of our Insurance Entities’ business, primarily distributes policies through our independent agency network and offers the following types of personal residential insurance: homeowners, renters/tenants, condo unit owners, and dwelling/fire.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in 10-K Item 1 Business and Q3 2026 10-Q Item 2 MD&A.
business_model.claim: The Insurance Entities sell policies across 19 states and hold an additional license in Tennessee, with Florida generating 72.6% of direct premiums written in 2025 and approximately 70.7% in the 2026 nine-month period.
quotes: During 2025, 72.6% of our overall direct premiums written were in Florida.

Although Florida represented approximately 70.7% of direct premiums written for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, it represented approximately 46.2% of total insured value as of September 30, 2026.

business_model.claim: Policies are distributed primarily through a network of approximately 9,500 licensed independent agents (3,900 in Florida) and also through direct-to-consumer online channels including wholly-owned digital agency Clovered, which partners with 39 third-party carriers.
quotes: We market and sell our products primarily through our network of approximately 9,500 licensed independent agents (3,900 in Florida).

As a personal lines property and casualty insurance agency, Clovered also partners with third-party insurance carriers and offers a wide suite of property and casualty insurance products, allowing us to earn non-risk bearing commission revenue for placing insurance on their behalf.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in 10-K Item 1 and Item 7 and Q3 2026 10-Q Item 2.
business_model.claim: UVE's vertically integrated service subsidiaries—ERA, BARC, Alder, and Wicklow—manage underwriting, inspections, reinsurance placement, and claims handling while generating non-risk-bearing fee and commission revenue.
quotes: Other sources of revenue include: commissions paid by our reinsurers to our reinsurance intermediary subsidiary BARC on reinsurance it places for the Insurance Entities; policy fees collected from policyholders by our managing general agent subsidiary, ERA; and financing fees charged to policyholders who choose to defer premium payments reflected in other income.

Our vertically integrated operating model includes the Insurance Entities and affiliated service companies that support key aspects of the insurance value chain, including product design, distribution, underwriting, risk management, claims administration and other operational functions.

quotes: We generate revenue primarily from the collection of insurance premiums.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in 10-K Item 7, Q3 2026 10-Q Item 2, and Q3 2026 earnings release.
business_model.claim: Premium volume is driven by policies in force (reaching 953,611, up 7.9% year-over-year), state rate changes, insured values, retention, and non-Florida expansion, with direct premiums written seasonally highest in the second and third quarters.
quotes: The amount of direct premiums written tends to be highest in the second and third quarters of our fiscal year and lowest in the first and fourth quarters.

Looking ahead, management expects business trends to be shaped by competition for new business and policy growth, retention rates for renewal business, the impact of rate changes, insured-value growth, claim frequency and severity, reinsurance costs, and operating efficiency.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in 10-K Item 1 and Item 1A and Q3 2026 earnings release.
business_model.claim: Reinsurance is one of UVE's most significant costs, resulting in a 30.3% ceded premium ratio in the 2026 nine-month period and depending on global reinsurance market pricing, weather history, and FHCF coverage.
quotes: In most years, reinsurance coverage is one of the most significant costs we incur.

Market conditions and public policy decisions beyond our control determine the availability and cost of the reinsurance we purchase and the ability of the FHCF to reimburse insurers at levels contemplated by their reimbursement contracts.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in Q3 2026 10-Q income statement, Q3 2026 earnings release, and 10-K Item 1A and Item 7.

quotes: We continue to see pressure on claim costs, driven by labor shortages, rising material costs, and the impact of tariffs.
The Insurance Entities’ loss and LAE experience on Florida claims has improved significantly for policies written after the statutory reforms.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in Q3 2026 10-Q income statement, Q3 2026 earnings release, and 10-K Item 1 and Item 7.

quotes: Policy acquisition costs and other operating costs and expenses include such items as underwriting costs, facilities, and corporate overhead.
We utilize an attractive commission-based compensation plan as an incentive for independent agents to place business with us.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in 10-K Item 1 and Q3 2026 10-Q Item 2.
business_model.claim: As a holding company, UVE's cash flows rely on dividends and permissible intercompany payments from its subsidiaries, which face regulatory oversight of statutory capital, investments, and affiliate transactions.
quotes: UVE is a holding company and, consequently, its cash flow is dependent on dividends and other permissible payments from its subsidiaries.
Regulatory oversight of the Insurance Entities extends to transactions and arrangements with the affiliated service companies that are part of our vertically integrated group.

competitive_position.claim: UPCIC is one of the largest residential property insurers in Florida, where UVE generated 72.6% of direct premiums written in 2025 and 70.7% through September 30, 2026.
quotes: As a result, UPCIC is one of the largest residential property insurers in Florida.
During 2025, 72.6% of our overall direct premiums written were in Florida.

Although Florida represented approximately 70.7% of direct premiums written for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, it represented approximately 46.2% of total insured value as of September 30, 2026.

competitive_position.claim: UVE operates a vertically integrated holding company model whose affiliated service companies perform product design, distribution, underwriting, risk management, inspections, reinsurance brokerage, and claims administration.
quotes: We are a vertically integrated holding company offering property and casualty insurance and value-added insurance services.

Our vertically integrated operating model includes the Insurance Entities and affiliated service companies that support key aspects of the insurance value chain, including product design, distribution, underwriting, risk management, claims administration and other operational functions.

competitive_position.claim: UVE distributes its policies through approximately 9,500 licensed independent agents, including 3,900 in Florida, alongside its wholly-owned digital agency Clovered.com, which partners with 39 carriers.
quotes: We market and sell our products primarily through our network of approximately 9,500 licensed independent agents (3,900 in Florida).

We have made substantial efforts in recent years to innovate across all of our service businesses, including continued development of our digital agency Clovered.com, where we have 39 carrier partners, and utilization of digital applications where applicable to administer claims.

competitive_position.claim: UVE's primary insurance subsidiaries, UPCIC and APPCIC, are rated "A" by Demotech and "A-" by Kroll, supported by approximately $509.1 million in combined statutory capital and surplus at year-end 2025.
quotes: Our Insurance Entities, UPCIC and APPCIC, are both currently rated “A” (“Exceptional”) by Demotech, Inc. (“Demotech”) and “A-” by Kroll Bond Rating Agency (“Kroll”), which are rating agencies specializing in evaluating insurer financial strength and stability.
Our combined statutory capital and surplus was approximately $509.1 million at December 31, 2025.

A downgrade in our financial strength or stability ratings may have an adverse effect on our competitive position, the marketability of our product offerings, and our liquidity, operating results and financial condition.

competitive_position.claim: UVE's policies in force grew 7.9% year-over-year to 953,611 as of September 30, 2026, while its net combined ratio improved to 91.0% from 96.4% in the prior-year quarter.
quotes: “Our net loss ratio continues to improve and new business trends are solid, including 8% growth in policies in force.”

competitive_position.claim: UVE has expanded outside Florida across 19 states, with non-Florida direct premiums written increasing 24.3% in 2025 to represent 27.4% of total direct premiums written.
quotes: We currently transact insurance in 19 states.
Direct premiums written for states outside of Florida increased 24.3%, representing a $114.7 million increase during 2025.

competitive_position.claim: UVE maintains high year-over-year policyholder retention and leveraged improved post-2022 Florida claim trends to cut Florida homeowners rates by 1.5% in 2024 and 5.1% in 2025 while expanding writings.
quotes: The Insurance Entities historically have enjoyed a high policyholder retention rate from year to year, both prior to the reforms and currently.

In 2024, for Florida, UPCIC implemented new homeowners policy rates, resulting in an average rate decrease of 1.5% compared to previous rates, effective for new policies August 15, 2024 and renewal policies May 17, 2025.

In October 2025, UPCIC implemented new homeowners policy rates for new and renewal business policies, resulting in an average rate decrease of 5.1% compared to previous rates with an effective date of October 16, 2025.

In Florida, the combination of improved claim and litigation trends attributable to the 2022 statutory reforms, increased product availability, and a more competitive authorized market supported our decision to expand new homeowners’ writings in most territories, introduce additional coverage options and adjust rates, resulting in an overall average rate decrease.

competitive_position.claim: Strict regulation in personal residential homeowners insurance makes product differentiation difficult, creating low barriers to entry aside from regulatory capital and driving intense competition on price and customer experience.
quotes: The personal residential homeowners insurance industry is strictly regulated.

As a result, it is difficult for insurance companies to differentiate their products, which creates low barriers to entry (other than regulatory capital and other requirements) and in typical circumstances results in a highly competitive market based largely on price and the customer experience.

competitive_position.claim: UVE faces intensifying competition from large national insurers, regional insurers, expanding incumbents, and a reported 17 new insurers that have entered Florida's normalizing market.
quotes: In many of the states in which we write business, we compete with small or regional insurers that might have greater familiarity with the local markets than we do.
We also compete with large national insurers, many of which have substantial brand awareness, experience, and capital resources.
In addition, a reported 17 new insurers have entered the Florida market in recent years.
In Florida, market improvements due to statutory reforms in 2022 have resulted in increased competition and are moderating or reducing pricing.

competitive_position.claim: Florida's state-backed insurer Citizens holds a statutorily created, consumer-subsidized pricing advantage in rising-rate environments because its annual rate changes are capped by law.
quotes: Citizens’ rate changes are limited by law, and accordingly, in times of rising insurance rates its premiums can significantly lag those of the authorized market.

This in turn causes Citizens to increasingly become the low-cost option for many policyholders; in essence, in hard markets Citizens has a statutorily-created, and ultimately consumer-subsidized, pricing advantage over authorized insurers operating in the state, including the Insurance Entities.
All together, renewed activity among authorized insurers has led to a decrease in Citizens’ policy count by approximately one million policies since the reforms.

competitive_position.claim: UVE relies on independent agents who control the primary customer relationship and are not obligated to promote UVE's policies over competing carriers.
quotes: These independent insurance agents maintain the primary customer relationship.
Independent agents typically represent other insurance companies in addition to representing us, and such agents are not obligated to sell or promote our products.
Other insurance companies may pay higher commissions than we do, provide services to the agents that we do not provide or adapt to evolving technologies faster than we do.

competitive_position.claim: Rapid competitor adoption of artificial intelligence and machine learning in pricing, underwriting, and distribution could place UVE at a competitive disadvantage.
quotes: The emergence of AI or other machine learning technologies is likely to change the ways consumers and insurance agents shop for, evaluate and purchase insurance products in ways that are difficult to predict.

Our ability to implement or adjust to technological changes, especially regarding artificial intelligence (“AI”), may be limited, or we could introduce technology containing errors, which may trigger regulatory actions or put us at a competitive disadvantage.

competitive_position.claim: Cyclical property and casualty pricing exposes UVE to losing market share if it overprices risks, or suffering underwriting losses and surplus depletion if it underprices risks or faces regulatory rate delays.
quotes: We also could overprice our risks, thereby making our products relatively less attractive than other alternatives, thereby negatively impacting our competitive position and potentially leading to a reduction in demand for our products and in our market share.

As a result, we could underprice risks, which, in the past, has and, in the future, could result in significant underwriting losses negatively impacting the profitability and financial condition of our Insurance Entities and the consolidated group.

competitive_position.claim: Concentration in Florida and coastal areas exposes UVE to severe hurricane and climate-related losses, potential erosion of statutory surplus, and dependence on reinsurance availability and pricing.
quotes: Because of our concentration in Florida, and in particular, in Broward, Palm Beach and Miami-Dade counties, we are exposed to hurricanes, windstorms, and other catastrophes affecting South Florida.
Catastrophes have eroded, and in the future may erode, our statutory surplus or ability to obtain adequate reinsurance which could negatively affect our ability to write new or renewal business.

If we are unable to maintain our current level of reinsurance or purchase new reinsurance protection in amounts that we consider sufficient and at prices and terms that we consider acceptable, we would have to either accept an increase in our exposure to catastrophe losses, reduce our insurance writings, seek rate adjustments at levels that might not be approved or might adversely affect policy retention, or develop or seek other alternatives, which could have an adverse effect on our profitability and results of operations.

competitive_position.claim: Political risk that Florida could reverse its 2022 statutory reforms, lingering pre-reform litigated claims, and increased regulatory scrutiny of affiliate transactions threaten UVE's cost structure and capital flexibility.
quotes: Over time, these political or external influences can result in policymakers questioning the merits of the reforms, considering proposals to reverse them, or pursuing other law changes or interpretations that could negate improvements in the Florida market and renew concerns with rising costs and reduced availability.

However, while the number of remaining pre-reform claims has declined substantially, those claims typically involve costly litigation and are difficult to resolve due to Florida’s prior attorneys’ fee statute.
We continue to observe increased political and regulatory focus on affiliate relationships, protection of policyholders, and transparency of intercompany transactions.

competitive_position.claim: Geographic expansion into new states carries execution risks from unfamiliar markets, unexpected severe weather such as winter storms, and state-specific regulatory requirements.
quotes: For instance, the presence of major winter storms or other extreme weather events in states into which we have expanded, has, in some cases, constrained the effectiveness of our risk diversification strategy.
This lack of experience in certain new markets could affect our ability to price risks adequately and develop effective underwriting standards.
